facts.text: The study thermally aged as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy at intermediate temperatures.
Aging near 600°C was compared with aging near 750°C to probe embrittlement and subsequent ductility recovery.
The ductile-to-brittle transition occurred within an approximate aging-temperature window of 550–750°C.
Aging below approximately 550°C did not produce the reported embrittlement transition, whereas aging above approximately 750°C produced ductile recovery.
Aging at 600°C enhanced L12 chemical ordering in the FCC domains toward Ni3Al stoichiometry.
The embrittled condition contained jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries whose tips acted as stress-concentration and crack-initiation sites.
Increased antiphase-boundary energy and elastic modulus in the ordered domains restricted cross-slip and promoted planar slip and dislocation pile-ups.
At 750°C, reduced L12 ordering and the formation of ductile transition zones along B2/FCC phase boundaries enabled ductility recovery.
The reported embrittlement was associated with phase-boundary-mediated plastic instability rather than classical grain-boundary impurity segregation.
The alloy exhibited a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile response as the aging temperature increased.
The 600°C-aged sample had the lowest ductility, while the 750°C-aged sample regained ductility.
